findings.evidence: Lattice.lean:171-181 defines `hcomp`/`hbij` as local `have`s; BaseChange.lean:341 already exports the one-step-weaker `baseChange_apply_baseChange_apply_of_comp_eq_smul`, showing the file is the canonical home for exactly this material.
findings.fix: Export the general statement in `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/BaseChange.lean`, beside `baseChange_comp` and `baseChange_apply_baseChange_apply_of_comp_eq_smul`: `Representation.IntertwiningMap.bijective_baseChange_of_comp_eq_smul {r : R} (hgf : ∀ v, g (f v) = r • v) (hfg : ∀ w, f (g w) = r • w) (A) (hr : IsUnit (algebraMap R A r)) : Bijective (f.baseChange A)` (or the derived `Representation.Equiv`), and reduce the char-0 branch here to applying it.
findings.issue: `hbij` (lines 171-181) is general infrastructure hidden inside a proof: its statement mentions only `Representation`, `IntertwiningMap`, `baseChange`, `IsUnit` and `Bijective`, and nothing about `reductionK0`/`latticeDefect`. Consequence: the docstring at line 149 asserts "In characteristic zero the reductions are isomorphic", but the only exported form is the weaker equality of K-classes, so any consumer wanting the isomorphism (e.g. the `reduction`-to-`FDRep` functor the description says is coming in #12715) must redo the argument.

findings.evidence: Basic.lean:106-109 (`(e : ρ.Equiv σ)`, base-changes internally); Lattice.lean:182-184 (new) and Lattice.lean:102-104 (existing `latticeDefect_eq_reductionK0`) both bypass it via `reductionK0_def` + `ExactK0.of_congr`.
findings.fix: Add `reductionK0_congr_baseChange (e : (Representation.baseChange k ρ).Equiv (Representation.baseChange k σ)) : reductionK0 k ρ = reductionK0 k σ := ExactK0.of_congr (Representation.asModuleLinearEquivOfEquiv e).toFGModuleCatIso` to `LatticeDefect/Basic.lean`, restate `reductionK0_congr e := reductionK0_congr_baseChange (e.baseChange k)` through it, and use it at Lattice.lean:182-184 and Lattice.lean:102-104.
findings.issue: Incomplete characteristic API for `reductionK0`: `reductionK0_congr` (LatticeDefect/Basic.lean:106-109) only accepts an `Equiv` of the ℤ-representations, so an `Equiv` of the already base-changed representations forces `rw [reductionK0_def, reductionK0_def]; exact ExactK0.of_congr (asModuleLinearEquivOfEquiv _).toFGModuleCatIso`. The same unfolding appears twice in this file.

summary: The characteristic-zero argument's general content — that an intertwining map whose composites are a scalar unit becomes bijective after base change — is buried in local `have`s instead of being exported next to its two companions in BaseChange.lean, so the stronger isomorphism the docstring advertises is unavailable to consumers. Relatedly, `reductionK0` lacks a congruence lemma for equivalences of the already base-changed representations, which is why the new proof (and the neighbouring one) unfolds `reductionK0_def`.
